newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl's party ready to let tax bill fail.
newsitem.headline: Kohl's party ready to let tax bill fail.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrat party (CDU) threatened on Monday to let this year's tax bill fail if it cannot reach a compromise deal with the opposition Social Democrats (SPD) on the measure.

CDU general secretary Peter Hintze told reporters that the bill -- already voted down by the SPD-controlled Bundesrat upper house -- would be dropped completely if no genuine compromise could be reached in parliament's mediation process.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel's tax package is a key element in financial plans for next year intended to enable Germany to meet the Maastricht treaty's budget deficit target and qualify for European monetary union scheduled for 1999.
The governing coalition wants to scrap wealth and property transaction taxes, but is deadlocked with the SPD. "These taxes must go," Hintze said after a meeting of CDU leaders.
He added that the SPD would be responsible for major losses in revenues if the tax bill fails to become law.

Waigel, sidelined on Monday by a cold, faces a tough week to try and salvage his tax bill. He must also get his 1997 austerity budget through the Bundestag lower house, where a final vote will be held on Friday.
